title: Drift test relating skills/quest/SKILL.md to questSkillContent
description: ADR gap 3, at opum-doc main 2112fc6, docs/adr/distribute-lore-and-quest-agent-skills-through-the-plugin-marketplace.md (operator ruling 2026-09-25T14:09:02.971Z, dispatched by opum-agent as OPAG-421). The plugin-shipped skills/quest/SKILL.md is kept by hand and deliberately differs from the generated questSkillContent (agent-instructions.ts:244): it is a shorter pointer that says it installs from the plugin. No test relates the two; test/contract/bootstrap-process.test.ts only checks the generated .claude/skills/quest/SKILL.md. Model it on lore-cli test/plugin-skill.test.ts. The copies need not be byte-identical, but the relationship must be asserted.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A test fails when skills/quest/SKILL.md and questSkillContent diverge on anything the relationship is defined to share (at least the frontmatter name and description, and each command they point to)
The test is shown to go red on a deliberate drift in each asserted part and green on the clean tree

plan: 1. Generate both skill variants from one function, questSkillDoc("repo"|"plugin"), keeping questSkillContent byte-identical to today so no installed repo copy drifts
2. The plugin variant reproduces the committed skills/quest/SKILL.md exactly; test asserts committed === questSkillDoc("plugin"), on the model of lore-cli test/plugin-skill.test.ts at 3ef3125
3. Assert both variants share the frontmatter and that every quest instructions topic they cite is a served guide
4. Prove red on a deliberate drift in each asserted part, green on the clean tree; bun run check
implementationNotes: Implemented. Both skill copies now come from questSkillDoc("repo"|"plugin") in agent-instructions.ts. They differ only in the provenance sentence, and questSkillContent = questSkillDoc("repo") is byte-identical to origin/dev c76bfc8 (compared by importing both), so no installed repo copy drifts. REAL DRIFT FOUND AND FIXED: the committed skills/quest/SKILL.md named two instruction files (CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md) where the CLI names three, omitting GEMINI.md. It is regenerated by scripts/plugin-skill.mjs --write, and the script with no flag exits 1 on drift. Test test/qcli372-plugin-skill-drift.test.ts, modelled on lore-cli test/plugin-skill.test.ts at 3ef3125, has 7 cases: the committed copy equals the plugin variant; questSkillContent equals the repo variant; the variants differ only in provenance; and for each variant, every cited `quest instructions <guide>` is served by findQuestGuide and every targetable instruction file is named. CONTROLS, each with a predicted subset: A, the pre-fix committed copy: 1/7 red, the committed-copy case. B, a guide misspelled in the generator: 3/7 red, the committed copy plus both guide cases. C, GEMINI.md dropped from the shared bullet: 3/7 red, the committed copy plus both instruction-file cases. Clean tree: 7/7. The first attempt at B left the file unchanged, because sed ran against the escaped backticks in the source; it was caught by the all-green result and re-run on the right line. bun run check exit 0, 617 pass.
finalSummary: The opum-quest plugin skill (skills/quest/SKILL.md) and the repo skill quest agents writes (questSkillContent) are now both generated by questSkillDoc, and a test holds the committed plugin copy to the generator. That closes ADR gap 3 (opum-doc 2112fc6). The plugin copy had already drifted, omitting GEMINI.md, and is corrected. The repo copy bytes are unchanged. Verified by three mutation controls, each turning red exactly its predicted subset (1/7, 3/7, 3/7), a clean 7/7, and bun run check exit 0 (617 pass).
